web.main.text101: This mode applies to bots in every deal of this game. Human players bid independently.
web.main.text102: All-pass: all bots pass. Misère: the first bot in the deal bids misère, the others pass. Human players must also pass to obtain the selected game.
web.main.text108: Leningrad. In pool-based games the total target is pool length × number of players, with no individual assistance. In timed games, finish the current deal. Mountain and whists are doubled. Half-whist is allowed on 6 and 7, with rewhisting.
web.main.text109: In all-pass, taking zero tricks earns the current price in the pool. Declaring a game or failing a contract does not reset the sequence. Ending all-pass depends on the result and configured exit rules; misère is allowed at any exit level.
web.main.text110: The first two all-pass leads follow the talon; the third is led by the first hand. With four players, the talon may win a trick for the dealer. Dealer bonuses, if enabled, on contracts 6–10: an ace or KQ of one suit earns 1 whist trick, AK of one suit earns 2, two aces earn 3. No bonuses on misère or all-pass.
web.main.text111: Returning the talon to the dealer.
web.main.text112: After receiving the talon and before declaring the game, the declarer may press “Reveal talon”. The original two talon cards remain face-up by the dealer. Scoring is selected in the agreements: “2 whist tricks” credits the declarer against the dealer for two tricks (8, 16, 24, 32, 40 on contracts 6–10); “mountain” charges the dealer one trick in mountain points (4, 8, 12, 16, 20). The final contract price applies. Only the selected option is scored. Unavailable on misère or all-pass. Otherwise the talon is shown face-down during play.
